title: Transition-Aware Dynamic Small-Cell Sleeping with PRB-Feasible Reassociation for Energy-Efficient 5G NR HetNets
content: Small-cell sleeping requires reassociation decisions that respect receiving-cell radio-resource budgets. We formulate multi-slot small-cell activation and physical resource block (PRB)-aware association as a binary energy-minimization problem with link feasibility, capacity, state persistence, and ON/OFF transition costs. A deterministic stateful controller tentatively reassociates displaced users, checks link-specific PRB demand and network energy, and commits or rolls back each complete state change. Across 100 paired Monte Carlo realizations, energy savings relative to Always-On are 6.60–12.11% under uniform placement and 0.65–1.15% under balanced hotspots. Transition awareness reduces aggregate state changes by 15.2% for a 0.029% mean energy penalty; the reduction reaches 47.6% at a 15-min interval. Savings remain positive across nine power calibrations. The heuristic matches the solver-certified mixed-integer linear programming reference in 16 of 20 reduced instances, with a 0.277% mean energy gap and a 2.037% maximum gap. Demand perturbation δ = 0.2 produces 5.59% mean resource failure; a 2 dB channel-state-information error at λ = 1.20 under uniform placement produces a +0.0708 excess slot-level failure probability relative to Always-On. These results support auditable energy control within the evaluated abstraction while identifying the need for uncertainty-aware safeguards near capacity.
